## Summary

One-month-later live update on his long mean reversion model ("all rules shared"): **new out-of-sample equity high**. Headline stats over the period shown: **+35% CAGR, −10.6% max drawdown, average capital use only 15%**. He frames it as "a typical long mean reversion system trading Nasdaq 100 stocks," and teases "the same approach also works…" — the trailing t.co resolves to the tweet's own photo (no external target), so the also-works claim (presumably other universes) has no follow-through in-text.

- **This is the same system as [[2026-09-16-systematicpeter-15pct-exposure-nasdaq-mean-reversion]], one month later.** Same +35% CAGR headline, drawdown ticked from ~−11% to −10.6%, same ~15% average exposure. A public system still making OOS highs a month after capture is small but real persistence evidence — exactly what the queued replication task should weigh.
- **The open question from the prior capture is still open:** whether 35% CAGR is measured on deployed or total capital. The update repeats the ambiguity verbatim, so resolving the basis stays the first item of the rules-pull.
- Live instance of his publish-everything philosophy ([[2026-09-04-systematicpeter-why-publish-research]]): public rules, then unfiltered OOS equity updates.
- **Skepticism gates:** author-reported stats; the OOS window remains the friendly post-2022 Nasdaq regime; photo unopened (period shown, curve shape, trade count unverified); "the same approach also works" is unsubstantiated in-text; engagement stats null at capture.
- **No new task** — the existing Inbox task (pull public rules + code, resolve CAGR basis, open chart at orig res, size into the TAA replication queue) covers this system; this update folds into it (add: confirm the period the new chart covers).
